  • Reason: News watcher detected a report — "Pentagon commits $300 million in conditional loans to SpaceX rivals" (mezha.net · mlq.ai). The watcher linked it to no trigger (—). The report is an item to verify, not a basis for judgment (Source: data/spacex_watch.json due · mezha.net)
  • Reference share price: $143.16 — 2026-11-10 (Tue) close, same as the previous run. This is the second run of the same day and it is before the U.S. market open on 11/11, so there is no new close (Source: stockanalysis daily history, previous run's queried value)
  • Scope: Only what the event touches — background for Axis B (launch) and Axis E (federal contracts), one new trigger (T13). The remainder of the measurement-layer dues are echoes of events handled by the 11/05–11/11 runs, so only rechecks are done. No recalculation of probability or fair value (Source: prompts/monthly_run.md · state.triggers_next_12m)
Conclusion first: The headline's '$300 million' is not a single item but the sum of two conditional loan commitments from the Defense Department's Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) — ① Stoke Space $150 million (announced 2026-10-26, Cape Canaveral second launch pad · Nova Block 2) ② Rocket Lab $150 million (announced 2026-11-09, flight cadence after the first launch of the reusable Neutron). Both are commitments with financial, legal, technical, investment and due-diligence requirements remaining before financial closing, and the announcements give no interest rate or maturity. Neither vehicle has yet flown even once (Neutron first flight targeted for 2027 · Nova Block 2 first flight scheduled for 2029 — reported). There is no SpaceX 8-K or IR. The fact that the government has begun funding to widen defense launch supply beyond SpaceX is worth recording, but there is no milestone input → probability 25/50/25 · probability-weighted $32 · 29 milestone judgments no change. New trigger T13 (loan closing · competing vehicle first flight · formalization of Falcon 9 retirement · NSSL assignments) established (Source: Sections 1–4 below).
